Hi Marta / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand Acme Payments' scale and procurement process. Quick recap from our discovery + a few asks so we can loop Legal & Finance and get you set up quickly: 

Key points from call:
- You want Redwood for inference across customer-facing fraud models (multi-tenant) with 99th pct latency SLOs and predictable monthly spend.
- Procurement will determine whether purchase happens via PO (preferred) or corporate card for initial POC.
- Marketplace route (AWS Marketplace) is of interest if it shortens your vendor onboarding.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Acme will pay via PO or card for the initial contract (we can accept either). If PO, include the contact who generates POs and the expected PO cadence (monthly/quarterly).
2) Complete the attached vendor packet and return with your W-9 so Finance can start the supplier setup. I attached our Redwood vendor packet for your convenience.
3) If you prefer marketplace procurement, confirm whether your procurement team needs a marketplace listing or an invoice-based purchase.

Attachments included: redwood_vendor_packet_2026.pdf (vendor packet, supplier form) — see section 2 for required fields.

Recommended owners / timeline:
- Acme: procurement point-of-contact to return completed packet + W-9 (target: 3 business days).
- Redwood: Aisha (sales) / Evelyn (finance) to process supplier onboarding once docs received.

If it helps, Evelyn from our Finance team (cc'd) can run through the vendor packet over a quick call — happy to schedule.

Thanks,

Aisha Rahman

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below: 

> 1) PO vs card
We expect to use a PO for the full contract. For the POC we can do a corporate card to speed things up, but procurement will push for PO by the time we go to production. PO owner: Rajiv (cc'd). Expected cadence: monthly.

> 2) Vendor packet + W-9
Attaching our completed onboarding form and our W-9. One note: Acme operates as an international entity for some payments, do you need a W-8BEN-E or only W-9 for U.S. tax reporting?

> 3) Marketplace
We are interested in AWS Marketplace if Redwood is already listed — that would make approvals quicker. If not, PO is fine.

Next steps from our side: Rajiv will open a ticket with procurement to start the PO flow; he estimates 7–10 business days once your packet is accepted.

Attachments: Acme_W9.pdf, acme_vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx

Hi Marta / Rajiv —

Thanks for sending the onboarding form and W-9 — I see the attachments and will start the supplier setup. A couple of clarifying items before we kick off: 

- Tax form: since Acme Payments is U.S.-registered per the W-9, we only need the W-9. If you later need cross-border invoicing we may request a W-8 series form.
- Banking info: for ACH payments we require a completed bank details form (bank_name, account_type, routing, account_number) or a voided check PDF. If you prefer wire, please confirm beneficiary details and intermediary bank specs.
- Vendor portal: once we create you as a supplier in our system, you will get an email with vendor portal access to upload banking docs securely.

Can you please confirm which payment method you prefer (ACH monthly invoices vs wire) and whether you'll accept electronic invoices? That will help us set payment terms (Net 30 standard).

I'll proceed to create the vendor record today and will share the portal invite — please do not email bank account numbers; use the portal once you receive the secure upload link.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Finance Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
Evelyn_hart@redwood.com
